title: Piano Sonata No. 23 in F minor, “Appassionata”
hook: Whispered threats, sudden eruptions and a finale that never stops running.

painting.title: An Eruption of Vesuvius
painting.collection: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
painting.pairingNote: A volcano bursts into fire above a dark, still bay; the sonata works the same way, long stretches of tense quiet broken by sudden explosions.

facts: Beethoven wrote it mostly in 1804 and 1805, the years of the *Eroica* Symphony and his opera *Fidelio*. It was published in Vienna in February 1807 and dedicated to his friend Count Franz von Brunsvik, a cellist.
The name “Appassionata”, “impassioned”, is not his. A publisher put it on a four-hand arrangement in 1838, eleven years after Beethoven’s death, and it stuck.
It pushes the piano of the time to its limits. The first movement keeps returning to the lowest F that Beethoven’s instruments had, and its closing pages sweep across almost the whole keyboard.
Much of it is quiet. The first movement begins almost in a whisper, and the loudest outbursts come without warning out of that quiet.
bigPicture.inOneLine: a whisper and an eruption (I), a calm hymn with variations (II), a whirlwind that ends in the minor (III).

movements.heading: Allegro assai
movements.summary: A movement in [[sonata-form|sonata form]] built on contrast: whispered phrases in bare octaves, then sudden crashes of sound across the keyboard. A small knocking figure in the bass keeps threatening, and the long [[coda|coda]] ends not in triumph but in a fading growl.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 1
mainIdeas.description: a broken chord that falls and rises in a dotted rhythm, both hands two octaves apart, very quiet. It is played again one step higher.

mainIdeas.name: The knock
mainIdeas.description: four low notes, three short and one long, the rhythm that opens the Fifth Symphony.

mainIdeas.name: Theme 2
mainIdeas.description: a warm, hymn-like melody in A-flat major over a pulsing bass. Its shape echoes theme 1, turned to the major.

stops.hear: Very quiet, both hands far apart in bare octaves: a falling and rising figure, then the same again a step higher
stops.happening: Theme 1, in [[unison|unison]]. The step up is the first jolt

stops.hear: Low in the bass, four notes knock softly: short-short-short-long
A pause, then a crash of loud chords racing up and down the keyboard
A warm, singing tune in chords over a steady, repeated bass note
Dark, falling runs in fast notes, loud and agitated
stops.happening: The end of the [[exposition|exposition]], in A-flat minor

stops.hear: The opening theme again, but in a bright, distant key
stops.happening: The [[development|development]]. There is no repeat of the exposition

stops.hear: Torrents of broken chords pour down and up the keyboard, louder and louder
The opening theme returns over a low note throbbing in quick repeated notes
The opening theme once more, building; then cascades of broken chords across the whole keyboard
Faster: the hymn-like theme 2, now loud and fierce, driven on by the left hand

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The storm dies away into the lowest notes of the piano, *ppp*
stops.happening: The movement ends in a whisper

notice: Listen for the knocking figure. It keeps coming back, sometimes as a soft warning in the bass, sometimes hammered out.
The same theme has several faces: whispered at the start, a hymn in theme 2, a shout in the coda.

movements.heading: Andante con moto
movements.summary: A calm set of [[variation|variation]]s on a simple, hymn-like theme in D-flat major. Each variation moves faster than the one before, then the theme returns in its plain form. The peace is broken at the very end.

mainIdeas.name: The theme
mainIdeas.description: slow chords low in the middle of the keyboard, with very little melody; each half is played twice.

mainIdeas.name: The variations
mainIdeas.description: the same harmony with faster and faster notes around it, rising higher on the keyboard.

stops.hear: Soft, dark chords low in the keyboard, almost like a hymn sung by low voices
The same chords, but the left hand now plays just after the beat, giving a gentle limp
A flowing line of quicker notes in the right hand, a little higher
Fast rippling notes, high and bright; the hands take turns with the theme and the ripple
The plain chords of the theme return, but each phrase jumps between low and high
A quiet, unsettled chord, then the same chord hammered loud
stops.happening: The music breaks off and goes straight into the finale

notice: Listen to the pace of the notes. The harmony barely changes from variation to variation; what changes is how fast the notes move: slow, then twice as fast, then faster again.

notes.title: No pause
notes.body: The finale follows without a break. On Spotify it is a new track, but in the score the last chord of the Andante leads straight into the first bars of the finale.

movements.heading: Allegro ma non troppo – Presto
movements.summary: A long, almost unbroken stream of fast notes in F minor, in [[sonata-form|sonata form]]. Unusually, Beethoven asks for the second half, not the first, to be played twice. A wild, faster [[coda|coda]] brings the sonata to a hard, tragic end.

mainIdeas.name: The alarm
mainIdeas.description: one loud, harsh chord hammered over and over.

mainIdeas.name: The whirl
mainIdeas.description: fast notes swirling in the right hand over short left-hand chords, the main theme.

mainIdeas.name: The Presto
mainIdeas.description: a new, stamping theme in heavy chords, then the whirl at top speed.

stops.hear: A loud chord struck again and again, then a cascade of fast notes tumbling down
stops.happening: The introduction: a call to arms

stops.hear: Quiet but restless: fast notes swirl in the right hand over light chords in the left
The swirl grows louder, with sharp accents and a more urgent idea
stops.happening: The second group, in C minor

stops.hear: The swirl moves to new keys; its pieces are passed between the hands
stops.happening: The [[development|development]] begins. Beethoven marks everything from here to the coda to be repeated

stops.hear: The main theme back in F minor
The music of ≈ 1:39 again
stops.happening: The repeat of the development and recapitulation

stops.hear: Faster still: a new, stamping tune in heavy chords, played twice

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: The whirl at full speed, then broken chords crashing down to the bottom of the keyboard

notice: The finale hardly stops for breath. Try to find a moment when the fast notes are not running.
Listen for the Presto’s new tune. It appears only once, and it sounds like a stamping dance.

notes.title: In this recording
notes.body: Gilels takes the long repeat of the second half, which is why his finale runs close to eight minutes. Without it, the movement lasts about five and a half.

threads.title: Quiet and loud
threads.body: All three movements live on sudden contrasts. The softest passages come right before the loudest.

threads.title: Low notes
threads.body: The low F in the first movement, the deep hymn in the second, the plunge to the bottom of the keyboard at the end: the sonata keeps going down.

threads.title: No way out
threads.body: The Andante’s hymn is broken by a single chord, and the finale ends in the minor. The calm at the centre does not last.
